summary: A husband who backed one candidate was banned from mentioning him at his wife's family Thanksgiving and held his tongue.
realLife: A Connecticut couple split between two 2016 candidates. The husband said he was barred from discussing his candidate at her family's Thanksgiving, and his wife said he really kept to himself. She was willing to talk with friends and neighbors, arguing a spouse can make the wrong choice and remain a good person. Both said they got support from others in divided households.
gates: The two spouses live in one household with opposite stands.
The in-laws' dinner has a no-politics rule.
weights: The in-laws' hostility to the other side.
inGame: Households, spouse ties and stands are on record; needs: a house rule for a gathering.

turns.what: He argues anyway and the wife leaves the table.
He stays quiet but a relative provokes him.
The rule loosens by the next holiday once tempers cool.
